source.title: AI/semis evening brief, Oct 26: 63 updates, 25 high [part 1/2]
source.body:
# Anthropic files to go public, and AI supply chains rally on the strength of its spending

**The bottom line:** Anthropic's IPO filing gave markets their first audited look at what a frontier lab spends on compute: $8.9 billion in just the first half of 2026. That spend lands with the chip, memory and optics suppliers. On the same day, Amazon said AWS capacity is sold out through 2027, Lumentum said its optical capacity is booked into 2029, and Celestica guided to roughly doubling revenue next year. Demand is not the open question. Financing is: more of the build-out is now funded by debt and equity raises.

## Anthropic's S-1: a renter of compute, not an owner

Anthropic, the maker of the Claude models, filed its prospectus on Monday to list on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E8TJMZeVtHs)). The key line for the supply chain is compute and infrastructure expense. It was $7.3 billion for all of 2025 and $8.9 billion for the first six months of 2026. Spending on its own property and equipment was only $482 million. Anthropic rents its compute from cloud providers rather than building it ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E8TJMZeVtHs)).

The headline net loss of $80.7 billion looks alarming but is mostly accounting. A $72.4 billion non-cash charge on convertible notes explains why the company still reported positive operating cash flow ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E8TJMZeVtHs)). Chinese outlet CLS reports H1 2026 revenue up more than 13x year on year ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2515964?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).

CLS also reports a listing around November 16 and more than $600 billion of future infrastructure commitments ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2515835?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). Both figures are reported, not confirmed.

On valuation, the last funding round valued Anthropic at $965 billion. Some investors have floated $2 trillion for the IPO. Each of the seven founders holds about 1.4%, worth more than $13 billion apiece ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2515861?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). Dario Amodei's 2025 pay was about $17.96 million, mostly stock and options ([36Kr](https://36kr.com/newsflashes/4042865455502213)).

**Read-through:** Because Anthropic rents its compute, its bill flows to cloud providers such as Amazon (AMZN) and, through them, to GPU, memory and networking suppliers. A successful listing would give the lab public-market capital to keep honouring those commitments. Markets read it that way: SK Hynix rose more than 6% at the open on the filing ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2515945?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).

## Demand is sold out; the question is who pays

Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said AWS compute capacity is essentially sold out through end-2027, with large orders stretching into 2028 ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2516093?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). That is the strongest demand signal of the period.

The funding side is shifting. Meta (META) plans to raise a total of $95 billion for AI infrastructure and its superintelligence push, and its stock fell 1.6% in early trading. Nvidia (NVDA), AMD (AMD) and Broadcom (AVGO) reportedly expressed interest in buying up to $5 billion of Meta stock ([36Kr](https://36kr.com/newsflashes/4043342836798597)). That would be suppliers helping fund a customer's purchases from them.

Sources disagree on the details:
- **Meta:** one report cites up to $950 million via stock sales, not $95 billion ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2515966?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).
- **SpaceX:** its GPU financing lease is reported as $40 billion by one outlet ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-27/detail-iniwrkkw2102981.d.html)) and about $400 billion by another ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2515966?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).

Treat both as unconfirmed until filings appear.

Bank forecasts point the same way. A Yahoo Finance segment puts Big Tech's 2027 AI capex at $1.2 trillion. JPMorgan puts hyperscaler spending above $1.1 trillion, and Goldman Sachs expects about one-third to be debt-funded ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rqlvkSPkTIQ)).

The counterpoint came from Apollo's chief economist Torsten Sløk. He found revenue per worker rising in tech but flat elsewhere, with no margin expansion outside tech so far ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jEwMFxOR0Ls)). If AI buyers outside tech don't see returns, debt-funded capex becomes the weak link.

## Korea's memory makers ride the wave into earnings week

Korean chip stocks rallied hard. Samsung (005930.KS) rose 4.9% and SK Hynix (000660.KS) 7.3% ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-27/detail-iniwrkkw2102981.d.html)), and the KOSPI opened up 3.46% ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2515945?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). Korean media report that SK Hynix will announce an extra 50–60 trillion won shareholder return plan alongside its October 28 earnings. Samsung reports October 31 ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-27/detail-iniwrkkw2102981.d.html)).

The macro data backs this up. Korea's Q3 GDP grew 1.0% quarter on quarter and 3.4% year on year, beating consensus of 0.8% and 3.1%, on AI-driven chip exports and investment. The Bank of Korea expects growth notably above prior forecasts and updates its outlook on November 26 ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2515916?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).

The same central bank also modelled the downside. In a pessimistic scenario where US tech giants cut AI capex, Korean chip exports could come in "USD 500 billion to 1 trillion" below forecast ([36Kr](https://36kr.com/newsflashes/4043525373285253)). That range looks implausibly large and may be a translation or unit error. The point stands that Korea's growth is now tied to US hyperscaler budgets.

RBC Capital expects the memory shortage to persist through 2027. It sees prices for HBM, the stacked high-bandwidth memory used next to AI GPUs, doubling in 2026, which supports overall DRAM selling prices, with SK Hynix the main beneficiary ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610273909462843.html)).

Further down the memory chain, Rambus (RMBS) also benefits. It makes interface and power-management chips for server memory modules and licenses memory IP. It posted record revenue of $218.3 million, up 22%, with product revenue of $114.3 million, and guided to "even stronger" Q4 ([SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/917273/000119312526431918/0001193125-26-431918-index.htm)).

## Optics and server builders: capacity booked for years

Celestica (CLS), a Toronto-based contract manufacturer that builds networking switches and AI server racks for hyperscalers, delivered the period's standout numbers:
- **Q3:** revenue up 83% to $5.83 billion.
- **2026 guidance:** raised to $21 billion.
- **2027 initial guidance:** $40 billion of revenue at a record 9% adjusted operating margin.
- **Beyond:** its CEO said customer forecasts for 2028 are "meaningfully higher" ([SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1030894/000103089426000049/0001047127-26-000049-index.htm)).

That is a direct read-across to suppliers of 800G and 1.6T networking.

Lumentum (LITE), a US maker of lasers and optical components, went further. Its CEO said capacity is booked through the start of 2029, customers are locking in 2030 supply, and about 70% of 2027 market demand will go unmet even with expansion ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2516106?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).

The comments lifted China's co-packaged optics (CPO) names. CPO puts optical links directly next to the chip. Innolight (300308.SZ), the largest maker of the transceivers that link AI servers, rose 4%+ in Hong Kong trading ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2516046?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). Ruiyuan's Growth Value Fund raised its Innolight stake by over 80% in Q3 ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610273909462031.html)).

China's statistics bureau shows how much money this is moving through the supply chain. In January–September:
- Optical fibre manufacturing profit rose 5.7x and optical cable 1.1x, on datacenter construction ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2516043?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).
- Electronic specialty materials profit grew 2.2x and semiconductor discretes rose 51.7% ([Tonghuashun](https://news.10jqka.com.cn/20261027/c681117842.shtml)).
- High-tech manufacturing profit rose 52% ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610273909251048.html)).

Smaller suppliers are feeling it too. Machine-tool maker Createch (300083.SZ) said nine-month new orders rose 77%. AI hardware, mainly liquid-cooling and optical-module makers, was the largest source at 25.5% of orders ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/300083/AN202610271831010970.html)). Guoci Materials (300285.SZ), a supplier of the ceramic powder used in MLCC capacitors (tiny components found throughout every server board), expects batch supply for AI-server grades in Q4 ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610273909234087.html)).

## Packaging and equipment: bonding is the new battleground

Applied Materials (AMAT) will lift its stake in Dutch assembly-equipment maker Besi (BESI.AS) to about 20%. Besi leads in hybrid bonding, which fuses chips directly copper-to-copper and is key for stacking HBM and chiplets. The partnership extends to thermo-compression bonding and die-on-wafer and die-on-panel integration. Applied says it won't go beyond ~20% or seek a board seat, and the deal awaits US antitrust (HSR) clearance ([SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/6951/000162828026067303/0001628280-26-067303-index.htm)). Applied is effectively locking in the advanced-packaging toolset that AI chips increasingly depend on.

Not everyone in packaging is keeping pace. Amkor (AMKR), the largest US-listed outsourced chip packager, missed on Q3 sales: $1.99 billion versus a $2.04 billion estimate. Its Q4 guide of $1.9–2.0 billion also trails the $2.05 billion consensus, despite record computing revenue and capex raised to about $2.5 billion ([SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1047127/000104712726000049/0001047127-26-000049-index.htm)). The mixed result suggests AI gains are not yet offsetting softness elsewhere in its business.

Jefferies expects the equipment boom to persist through 2028. It rates Applied and Lam Research (LRCX) Buy, and ASML (ASML) and Screen Holdings Hold ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610273909402132.html)). In China, chip-test equipment maker Changchuan Technology (300604.SZ) reported nine-month revenue up 57% and net profit up 104%, and plans a CNY 50–100 million buyback ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610273909431523.html)).

## China: model exports, compute build-out and robots

On policy, state media say DeepSeek and MiniMax have completed technology-export registration with the Commerce and Science ministries. That clears them for open-source releases and overseas licensing ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610263908186113.html)). Beijing is formalising oversight of model exports rather than blocking them. Hong Kong-listed model maker Zhipu jumped 10%+ ([Tonghuashun](https://news.10jqka.com.cn/20261027/c681118656.shtml)).

Compute is being built close to cheap power. Envision Group delivered phase one of its Ulanqab datacenter in Inner Mongolia. The site is planned for 3GW of load with 80% direct green power, and compute orders are booked into 2027 ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610273909462262.html)).

Robotics demand is growing, though the evidence so far is thinner:
- **Sales:** China's embodied-AI robot sales rose 22.6% in the first three quarters ([36Kr](https://36kr.com/newsflashes/4043296859837574)).
- **ByteDance:** it is hiring across robot hardware, dexterous hands and data ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2516058?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).
- **Toyota:** a single report says it plans to deploy 400,000 humanoids ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610273909419517.html)).

Component suppliers are still mostly at the sample stage. For now, the robot trade runs more on announcements than on orders.

## What to watch

- **SK Hynix (Oct 28) and Samsung (Oct 31) earnings:** HBM pricing commentary and whether the reported 50–60 trillion won return plan materialises.
- **Anthropic's roadshow and pricing, reportedly mid-November:** how the market values a lab that rents its compute, and whether the $600B+ commitment figure is confirmed.
- **Meta and SpaceX financing details:** the reported sizes conflict, and the debt share of AI capex is the key risk flagged by Goldman and Apollo.
- **Bank of Korea forecast update (Nov 26):** an early gauge of how exposed Korea is to any slowdown in US AI capex.
- **Besi deal clearance under HSR:** watch for rival moves to secure hybrid-bonding capacity.

# China (38)

## AI (10)

🔴 **[10-27 10:46 Beijing] Liang Wenfeng of DeepSeek enters China Rich List top ten with CNY 280 billion wealth**  
On 27 October, the Hurun Research Institute released the "2026 Hurun China Rich List". There are 1,529 entrepreneurs with personal wealth exceeding CNY 5 billion on the list, an increase of 95 compared to last year. Total wealth of those on the list is CNY 32 trillion, up 7% year-on-year. Zhang Yiming, founder of ByteDance, became China's richest person for the second time with CNY 670 billion in wealth, setting a new record. Liang Wenfeng of DeepSeek entered the top ten of the list for the first time with CNY 280 billion in wealth.  
_News · Sina · DeepSeek · [Source](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-27/detail-iniwrqsu2111752.d.html)_

🔴 **[10-27 08:19 Beijing] Anthropic IPO set for mid-November with $600B+ infrastructure commitments; Rokid AI glasses Gen 2 launches today**  
Anthropic reportedly plans IPO around November 16, with analysts bullish on company's $600B+ future infrastructure spending commitments that could open new markets. The company's optical module high-precision placement equipment has been delivered to customers. Rokid's second-generation AI glasses launch today; analysts view AI eyeglasses entering growth stage with domestic optics manufacturers accelerating to capture industry upside. Tesla rises 5.21%; Barclays upgrades to 'overweight' citing business momentum and SpaceX merger potential.  
_News · CLS · Anthropic,Rokid,Tesla · [Source](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2515835?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)_

**[10-27 11:02 Beijing] Citi reiterates Tencent target price HKD 755, 2026 Global Digital Ecosystem Conference as catalyst**  
Citi released a research note indicating the upcoming 2026 Global Digital Ecosystem Conference may serve as a potential catalyst for Tencent. The firm expects Tencent to announce the formal release of Hunyuan 4.0, share WorkBuddy operational milestones, and provide updates on Tencent Cloud infrastructure upgrades and global cloud expansion strategy. Despite current weakness in China's internet sector, Citi views recent stock weakness as a better buying opportunity for long-term investors. The firm maintains a "Buy" rating on Tencent with a constructive stance on AI agents, reiterating a target price of HKD 755.  
_News · Sina · Tencent (腾讯, 0700.HK) · [Source](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-27/detail-iniwrqsu2124361.d.html)_

## Semiconductors (13)

🔴 **[10-27 11:09 Beijing] Createch (创世纪) Q3 2026: AI hardware orders surge to CNY 19.97b; embodies 25.54% of total new orders**  
Createch Technology (创世纪, 300083) held an investor call on 26 October 2026. Key highlights:  
- 9M 2026: revenue CNY 54.472 billion (+42.38% YoY); net profit CNY 5.762 billion (+65.60% YoY); non-GAAP net profit CNY 5.799 billion (+70.10% YoY). Q3 alone: revenue CNY 22.426 billion (+61.98% YoY); net profit CNY 2.751 billion (+139.76% YoY).  
- 9M new orders CNY 78.209 billion (+77.22% YoY), exceeding full-year 2025. AI hardware (liquid cooling, optical modules) new orders CNY 19.974 billion (25.54% of total), the largest single order source; new energy (EVs, wind, solar) CNY 11.106 billion (14.20%); embodied robots CNY 4.666 billion (5.97%). Emerging sectors combined represent 45.71% of orders, significantly exceeding traditional 3C consumer electronics.  
- Contract liabilities CNY 10.447 billion at end-Q3, up 135.19% from year-start.  
- Q3 gross margin 25.25% (QoQ +1.44pp), net margin 12.27% (QoQ +0.99pp).  
- AI hardware clients concentrated in server and compute-hardware component manufacturing, including liquid-cooling and optical-module suppliers and downstream integrators. Competitive advantages: high customer overlap with 3C and EV bases; complete product line; flexible capacity.  
- Product lines serve high-end five-axis machine tools with growing domestic substitution in new energy and AI hardware. Embodied robotics orders in early volume-ramp phase, targeting joint, reducer, screw, gear, dexterous-hand, frame precision components.  
- Company operates micro-smile-curve model focusing on R&D and sales, outsourcing core parts; bases in Shenzhen (HQ), Dongguan, Suzhou, Huzhou, Yibin, and Vietnam (production started 2025, own factory under construction). Serves 50+ countries across SE Asia, Europe, LatAm.  
- 9M R&D expense CNY 115 million (+11.36% YoY), targeting spindle reliability and core parts like datums, high-precision rotary tables, and CNC system secondary development.  
_Filing · SSE/SZSE filing · Createch (创世纪, 300083) · [Source](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/300083/AN202610271831010970.html)_
